d: Every winter, stubble-burning fires across north India add to the region's pollution crisis. But in Uttar Pradesh's Shahjahanpur, once among the state's biggest farm-fire hotspots, the number of reported fires has fallen dramatically. The change has come by giving farmers alternatives. Industrial balers collect paddy straw and compress it into blocks that are sold to thermal power plants and compressed biogas factories. Other farmers use mulchers to mix the leftover stubble into the soil. Janaki Pande reports from Shahjahanpur on how one district brought down stubble-burning fires.
